description: 1. Agent discovers memory-guard CLI tool (via SKILL.md or by exploring /usr/local/bin). 2. Runs `memory-guard init` in /workspace, which creates .memory-guard/hashes.json with SHA-256 hashes of SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, IDENTITY.md and their initialized_at/size metadata, and creates actions.log, rejections.log, handoffs.log (the proprietary three-log pattern). 3. Runs `memory-guard stamp <file>` on at least two memory files (e.g., MEMORY.md, HEARTBEAT.md), which adds the bespoke [agent|timestamp|confidence|rationale] provenance header — a proprietary format an agent cannot guess without reading the SKILL.md. 4. Modifies one of the tracked identity files (e.g., appends text to SOUL.md or AGENTS.md) to simulate tampering. 5. Runs `memory-guard verify` which detects the hash mismatch, logs the tampering detection to rejections.log, and prints an alert. 6. Runs `memory-guard audit` which produces the full change report and logs 'audit completed' to actions.log. The key proprietary traps are: (a) the specific .memory-guard/hashes.json registry path and structure, (b) the [agent|timestamp|confidence|rationale] stamp format, (c) the three-log pattern of actions.log/rejections.log/handoffs.log being auto-created on init.
